metadata.title: C172 JT-A Systems Trainer
metadata.studyNotice: Placeholder/simplified data is used where exact aircraft-specific details are not yet entered. Do not use as POH/AFM, checklist, maintenance, or operating guidance.

systems.name: Electrical System
systems.summary: Buses, battery, alternator/generator logic, essential power paths, and annunciations.

systems.name: Fuel System
systems.summary: Simplified Jet-A feed and return concept for learning source selection, pumps, filtering, rail/injector flow, and fault consequences.

components.name: Left Tank
components.what: Stores Jet-A fuel and supplies the selector when the left source path is selected or available.
components.failure: A leak, contamination, or unusable fuel condition reduces available source fuel and may force use of another source if available.
components.normal: Fuel available, venting assumed normal, and the path available when selected.
components.abnormal: Fuel imbalance, low usable fuel, contamination signs, or loss of feed from the selected side.

components.name: Right Tank
components.what: Stores Jet-A fuel and supplies the selector when the right source path is selected or available.
components.failure: A leak, contamination, or unusable fuel condition reduces available source fuel and may force use of another source if available.
components.normal: Fuel available, venting assumed normal, and the path available when selected.
components.abnormal: Fuel imbalance, low usable fuel, contamination signs, or loss of feed from the selected side.

components.name: Fuel Selector
components.what: Routes fuel from the selected tank path toward the pump and filter side of the system.
components.failure: Incorrect selection or blockage can remove the intended fuel source from the feed path.
components.normal: Selected source has a clear route downstream.
components.abnormal: Unexpected low fuel pressure, imbalance, or feed from the wrong side.

components.name: Electric Fuel Pump
components.what: Provides auxiliary pressure support in this simplified concept model.
components.failure: Loss of auxiliary pressure support may increase reliance on downstream engine-driven pumping.
components.normal: Available and able to support steady fuel flow when commanded.
components.abnormal: Fuel pressure messages, abnormal pump behavior, or reduced margin if another pump is degraded.

components.name: Fuel Filter
components.what: Removes contaminants before fuel reaches higher-pressure/engine fuel metering areas in this concept layout.
components.failure: Restriction reduces available flow and can create downstream pressure drop.
components.normal: Clean enough to pass required flow.
components.abnormal: Reduced fuel pressure/flow margin, engine roughness risk, or caution indications in a final aircraft-specific model.

components.name: Engine Driven Pump
components.what: Provides engine-driven fuel feed pressure to the high-pressure stage in this simplified trainer.
components.failure: Loss may remove the primary mechanical feed path and can cause fuel pressure decay depending on backup availability.
components.normal: Supplies stable downstream pressure while the engine is operating.
components.abnormal: Low pressure, engine power loss, rough running, or FADEC-related messages in a more exact model.

components.name: High Pressure Pump
components.what: Raises pressure for the common rail and injector side in this simplified diesel engine concept.
components.failure: Insufficient rail pressure can prevent correct injection and may lead to power loss or engine shutdown.
components.normal: Builds and maintains rail pressure within commanded range.
components.abnormal: Rail pressure low/high indications, rough running, reduced power, or FADEC fault messages.

components.name: Common Rail
components.what: Distributes high-pressure fuel to injectors and supports the FADEC-commanded injection mental model.
components.failure: Pressure loss or sensor fault can affect all injectors and engine output.
components.abnormal: Rail pressure warnings, unstable power, or engine roughness.

components.name: Injectors
components.what: Meter fuel into the cylinders according to engine-control commands in this simplified model.
components.failure: Blocked, leaking, or incorrectly commanded injection can cause roughness, power loss, or abnormal engine parameters.
components.normal: Deliver commanded fuel quantity and timing.
components.abnormal: Rough running, EGT/engine-parameter abnormalities, smoke, or FADEC-related messages.

components.name: Engine
components.what: Consumes metered fuel and provides power to the propeller through the engine/propeller system.
components.failure: Fuel starvation, metering faults, or pressure loss can produce power loss or stoppage.
components.normal: Stable power for the selected single-lever/FADEC command.
components.abnormal: Power loss, roughness, abnormal temperatures/pressures, or engine alerts.

components.name: Return Line
components.what: Returns excess fuel from the rail/engine side toward the return/cooling path in this concept layout.
components.failure: A blocked return path can increase pressure or temperature stress depending on actual system design.
components.normal: Excess fuel has a managed route back through the return side.
components.abnormal: Fuel temperature or pressure cautions in a final aircraft-specific model.

components.name: Fuel Cooler / Thermostat
components.what: Placeholder for return-fuel temperature management. Replace with exact component name and routing when confirmed.
components.failure: Cooling or bypass malfunction could affect fuel temperature control.
components.normal: Return fuel temperature is managed before returning to tank/feed path as applicable.
components.abnormal: Fuel temperature caution, reduced thermal margin, or return-system fault indication.

scenarios.name: Normal Operation
scenarios.description: Both tank paths are available in this concept view. Fuel moves from source to selector, pumps, filter, rail, injectors, engine, and return path.
scenarios.consequence: Normal feed and return paths are active. Exact pump command logic should be updated from approved aircraft data later.

scenarios.name: Electric Fuel Pump OFF
scenarios.description: The auxiliary pump is not running. The concept shows continued reliance on downstream engine-driven pumping.
scenarios.consequence: Study note: loss of auxiliary pressure support may reduce system margin. Use approved procedures in real operations.

scenarios.name: Fuel Filter Restricted
scenarios.description: The filter creates a downstream restriction and reduces available flow/pressure margin.
scenarios.consequence: Study note: a restriction can show as pressure/flow loss and may affect engine power. This is not a checklist.

scenarios.name: Tank Selected LEFT
scenarios.description: Only the left source path is selected in this simplified model.
scenarios.consequence: Study note: the right feed path is greyed out. Watch source management and imbalance concepts.

scenarios.name: Tank Selected RIGHT
scenarios.description: Only the right source path is selected in this simplified model.
scenarios.consequence: Study note: the left feed path is greyed out. Watch source management and imbalance concepts.

scenarios.name: Engine Driven Pump Failure
scenarios.description: The main mechanical feed pump is failed in this concept view.
scenarios.consequence: Study note: downstream pressure/rail supply may be lost or degraded. Treat responses as placeholders until aircraft-specific procedures are entered.

faults.name: Fail Electric Fuel Pump
faults.pilotIndication: Possible fuel pressure caution or reduced backup/auxiliary pressure margin.
faults.risk: Less pressure support if another part of the feed system is degraded.
faults.response: Study note: identify the failure, monitor engine/fuel indications, and use approved aircraft procedures.

faults.name: Restrict Fuel Filter
faults.pilotIndication: Possible low fuel pressure/flow cues, rough running, or reduced power in a final aircraft-specific model.
faults.risk: Downstream starvation or inability to maintain commanded rail pressure.
faults.response: Study note: recognize restriction signs and follow the approved abnormal procedure.

faults.name: Fail Engine Driven Pump
faults.pilotIndication: Likely fuel pressure/engine power abnormality in this concept model.
faults.risk: Loss of downstream feed pressure and possible power loss.
faults.response: Study note: maintain aircraft control, diagnose with indications, and use approved emergency/abnormal guidance.

faults.name: Block Return Line
faults.pilotIndication: Possible fuel temperature/pressure abnormality if modeled by exact aircraft data.
faults.risk: Return-side pressure or temperature control may be compromised.
faults.response: Study note: monitor relevant indications and apply approved aircraft guidance.

faults.name: Select Left Tank Only
faults.pilotIndication: Fuel use is focused on the selected side in this simplified model.
faults.risk: Fuel imbalance or depletion of the selected source if not managed.
faults.response: Study note: verify selection and manage fuel according to approved procedures.

faults.name: Select Right Tank Only
faults.pilotIndication: Fuel use is focused on the selected side in this simplified model.
faults.risk: Fuel imbalance or depletion of the selected source if not managed.
faults.response: Study note: verify selection and manage fuel according to approved procedures.

memoryMode.instructions: Click the tiles in the order you remember fuel flowing from selected tank to engine. Either tank can count as the selected tank for the first position.

oralQuestions.prompt: Explain what happens if the electric fuel pump fails.
oralQuestions.modelAnswer: Study answer: the auxiliary pump is unavailable, so the system has less pressure support and relies more on the remaining feed path. The pilot would monitor fuel/engine indications and use approved procedures rather than improvising from this trainer.

oralQuestions.prompt: Explain the fuel path from tank to injector.
oralQuestions.modelAnswer: Study answer: in this simplified model, fuel flows from the selected tank through the selector, electric fuel pump, filter, engine-driven pump, high-pressure pump, common rail, and then to the injectors.

oralQuestions.prompt: What components are affected by a restricted fuel filter?
oralQuestions.modelAnswer: Study answer: the filter restriction primarily affects downstream flow to the engine-driven pump, high-pressure pump, common rail, injectors, and ultimately engine power availability.

oralQuestions.prompt: What changes when only LEFT tank is selected?
oralQuestions.modelAnswer: Study answer: the left feed path remains active and the right feed path is inactive in this concept model. The pilot should think about selected source, fuel balance, and remaining usable fuel.
